name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.176.0 — The replay tree is the reviewed tree: each review now records the two commits bounding what it judged as refs under refs/spec-review/<runId>/ — judged at the close row's head sha, close at the close commit — written best-effort so a failed write can never block a close. The replay harness reads that pair instead of asking which commit last touched the spec file, refuses (exit 4) a row that cannot name its own bounds, and reconstructs the pre-ref backlog only through the new run-once replay.js --backfill-pins. Setup re-derives the target's own AC coverage against the tree it assembled and exits 5 with a diagnosis rather than printing a success line over a tree the review never saw. 7.175.0 — A wireframe now carries no styles of its own: it links only the three named stylesheet layers — the shared register, the shared kit, and the project's own kit — and a project's own vocabulary lives in that one file, which may not redefine or outgrow the shared kit it extends. Every design-atlas.js check run over a resolved project kit now prints its size against the shared kit's own, its rules used on exactly one screen, and its layout share — the proportion of its rules that are pure layout rather than styling, the number a deferred component-kit decision reads. 7.174.0 — Review close re-stamps the build ledger row's deviations count from the sidecar's final entry count. The build driver writes that count at COMMIT, so a sidecar restated into countable bullets afterwards left the row permanently under-reporting (specs/20260912/14 recorded 0 against two real entries); the count is only final once the fold happens, which is the close. The correction rewrites the last build row for that spec in place, touching only the number, and prints itself once in the step that follows the close.
